questions.explanation: Pay, career progression, and EMT well-being are the human resources department's job, not the medical director's.
questions.question: An EMT asks who handles her pay raise, her promotion path, and the agency wellness program. Which department is that?

questions.explanation: Well-being support, career progression, and compensation all sit in the human resources department.
questions.question: An EMT is burned out and asks about the employee assistance counseling benefit, how promotions work, and how pay steps are set. Which department handles all of that?

questions.explanation: Career progression and well-being are human resources matters; protocols belong to medical direction.
questions.question: A new EMT wants to know who to see about his career ladder and well-being support, not about a patient-care protocol. Who should he see?

questions.explanation: Obtaining continuing education is the individual EMT's own responsibility, not the training officer's or the medical director's.
questions.question: An EMT's certification expires in two months and his continuing education hours are short. Whose responsibility is it to get them done?

choices: To qualify for a pay step increase
To replace her initial EMT training
To satisfy her employer's scheduling requirement
To maintain, update, and expand her knowledge and skills
questions.explanation: Maintaining, updating, and expanding knowledge and skills is the stated purpose of continuing education in EMS.
questions.question: An EMT takes a new stroke-assessment class so her knowledge stays current and grows. What is the purpose of this education?

questions.explanation: The duty to obtain continuing education sits with the EMT personally, even when others offer the classes.
questions.question: An EMT blames the state bureau because nobody scheduled his refresher before his card lapsed. Who was responsible for obtaining that education?

choices: Accidental Death and Disability: The Neglected Disease of Modern Society
The National Scope of Practice Model
questions.explanation: The 1966 white paper exposed untrained attendants and ill-equipped ambulances and became the founding document of modern EMS. The other choices are later standards and education documents, not the 1966 report.
questions.question: Modern EMS in the United States is usually traced back to a single 1966 report by the National Academy of Sciences / National Research Council that exposed how inadequate ambulance care was at the time. What was that report?

choices: Accidental Death and Disability: The Neglected Disease of Modern Society
questions.explanation: The white paper used the 1965 injury and death figures to show prehospital care was a neglected public problem.
questions.question: Before 1966, a crash victim might get a ride with no trained care, and a report that year documented 107,000 accidental deaths in 1965. What document was it?
questions.topic: Accidental Death and Disability: The Neglected Disease of Modern Society

choices: Accidental Death and Disability: The Neglected Disease of Modern Society
The National EMS Agenda for the Future
questions.explanation: That National Academy of Sciences / National Research Council white paper is the origin point the textbook uses for modern EMS.
questions.question: An instructor asks which single 1966 publication started modern EMS reform. What do you name?
questions.topic: Accidental Death and Disability: The Neglected Disease of Modern Society

questions.explanation: The error came from missing knowledge about the drug, not from a broken rule or a slip of the hand.
questions.question: An EMT gives the wrong drug because she did not know what that drug does or when it is used. What kind of failure is this?

questions.explanation: He acted on knowledge he did not have, which is the definition of a knowledge-based failure.
questions.question: A provider picks a medication dose from memory, gets it wrong, and review shows he never learned the correct dose range. What kind of failure is this?

choices: A provider deliberately skips a required protocol step
A provider's gloved hand slips while starting an IV
A provider gives a drug without knowing its concentration
A provider's radio fails during a patient report
questions.explanation: Giving a drug without knowing its concentration means the pertinent knowledge was missing; knowingly breaking a rule is a rule-based problem.
questions.question: Which of these errors is a knowledge-based failure?

questions.explanation: Prehospital care standards and the people who provide that care are typically regulated by the state office of EMS.
questions.question: A new EMT asks who sets and enforces the standards for prehospital care and the providers who deliver it in her state. Who is it?

questions.explanation: Licensure, certification, and discipline of EMS providers sit with the state EMS authority, not hospitals or national organizations.
questions.question: An agency wants to know which office can discipline an EMT's state credential. Which one?

questions.explanation: State EMS offices authorize and regulate training programs, courses, and providers inside their state.
questions.question: A course director must get her EMT program and its continuing education courses approved before she can teach. Whose approval does she need?

choices: Proof of immunization against certain communicable diseases
questions.explanation: Proof of immunization is one of the criteria required to become licensed and employed as an EMT.
questions.question: A candidate has passed the EMT course and exam but has no vaccination record to show. Which requirement can still block her from being licensed and employed?

choices: Proof of immunization against certain communicable diseases
questions.explanation: Of those choices, proof of immunization is the textbook criterion for EMT licensure and employment.
questions.question: An applicant is offered four possible requirements and must pick the real one. Which is actually required for EMT licensure and employment?

choices: To bill the student's insurance for the vaccines
Because proof of immunization is required to become licensed and employed as an EMT
To decide which students get hospital rotations first
To complete the student's financial aid file
questions.explanation: Programs gather immunization proof up front because the credential and the job both depend on it.
questions.question: Before clinical rotations, a program collects each student's MMR, varicella, and hepatitis B records or positive titers. Why does it collect them?

choices: A rule-based failure, because she knowingly violated protocol
A knowledge-based failure, because she lacked knowledge about the medication
An equipment failure, because the bags were defective
A communication failure, because the hospital gave the wrong order
questions.explanation: The review named a knowledge deficit about the medication and called for education, not punishment.
questions.question: A crew treating a severely dehydrated patient hung a 250 mL bag of 10% dextrose instead of the intended normal saline; the two bags looked identical. The root-cause review found the provider did not appreciate the concentration she was administering. What type of failure did the review identify?

choices: Her agency must cover her shifts until she finishes
She receives an automatic six-month grace period
She must stop providing EMT services as of the certification expiration date
Only her agency is penalized, not the EMT
questions.explanation: Indiana puts the burden of demonstrating compliance on the individual EMT, who must stop providing EMT services if the requirements are unmet at expiration.
questions.question: An Indiana EMT's certification is nearing its two-year expiration and she has not completed the required 40 hours of continuing education. Under the state's instructions, what happens if she does not meet the requirement?

questions.explanation: State offices of EMS license, certify, and discipline individual providers and services, and the actions are public record.
questions.question: A state EMS office publishes its 2025 enforcement actions: one EMT's credential suspended, one EMR's revoked, and a correction order with a fine issued to an ambulance service. Which body carried out these actions?

choices: Human resources, which handles EMT compensation
questions.explanation: Compensation is one of the human resources department's three areas, and when pay lags, staffing and coverage fail next.
questions.question: Over 13 months, seven paramedics and three EMT officers resigned from a county EMS agency over lagging pay, and the director asked the county council to amend the salary ordinance so wages could be raised. Which area of responsibility does this problem fall under?

choices: Accidental Death and Disability: The Neglected Disease of Modern Society
questions.explanation: human resources department: The department that deals with the well-being of the EMT, career progression, and EMT compensation.
questions.question: Which term is defined as: The department that deals with the well-being of the EMT, career progression, and EMT compensation.

questions.explanation: The human resources department deals with the well-being of the EMT, career progression, and EMT compensation. The medical director handles medical care and protocols, not pay or wellness benefits.
questions.question: An EMT emails the medical director asking for a raise and for changes to the agency's employee wellness program. The medical director replies that pay and employee well-being are not his office's job. Which department handles them?

choices: The state office; it must extend his card while he catches up
His partner; partners share responsibility for each other's hours
His agency; it must pay him for the hours he missed
The EMT himself; he must complete the continuing education required to renew
questions.explanation: Continuing education is ongoing education each individual EMT is responsible for obtaining to keep certification. The agency, the state, and his partner cannot carry that responsibility for him.
questions.question: An EMT's certification lapses because his refresher hours were never finished. He insists his agency should have scheduled them for him. Who was responsible for getting that education done, and what fixes the lapse?

questions.explanation: Continuing education maintains, updates, and expands the knowledge of someone already certified, which is what an update course for a working EMT is. Initial training is what she completed before she was first certified.
questions.question: A certified EMT with three years on the job takes a short update course when her state adds a new skill to the EMT scope, so she can learn it and keep her knowledge current. This kind of training is:

choices: Most ambulances were ill-equipped, many were hearses, and attendants had little or no standard training
Ambulance crews were well trained but badly paid
Cities had far more ambulances than they could staff
Hospitals were refusing to receive ambulance patients
questions.explanation: The 1966 white paper documented that prehospital care was inadequate: vehicles doubled as hearses, equipment was minimal, and there was no standard for attendant training. That exposure is what launched modern EMS reform.
questions.question: In 1966, the National Academy of Sciences / National Research Council published a landmark report about trauma deaths in the United States. What did it expose about ambulance services at the time?
questions.topic: Accidental Death and Disability: The Neglected Disease of Modern Society

choices: Funeral homes took over most ambulance services across the country
Private ambulance companies were banned by the federal government
Attendant training requirements were dropped nationwide
Standards were set for ambulance design, equipment, and attendant training, backed by new federal programs
questions.explanation: The report's recommendations pushed the federal government to set standards for vehicles, equipment, and training and to fund EMS development. Ambulance care became more regulated afterward, not less.
questions.question: The 1966 white paper is credited with starting modern EMS. What changed in American ambulance care as a direct result of its recommendations?
questions.topic: Accidental Death and Disability: The Neglected Disease of Modern Society

choices: Accidental Death and Disability: The Neglected Disease of Modern Society
questions.explanation: Knowledge-based failure: An error that happens because the provider did not know the pertinent information — for example, giving the wrong drug because she did not know the information about that drug.
questions.question: Which term is defined as: An error that happens because the provider did not know the pertinent information — for example, giving the wrong drug because she did not know the information about that drug.

choices: A rule-based failure, because she knowingly broke a rule
A skill-based slip, because her hands fumbled a familiar task
questions.explanation: A knowledge-based failure happens when the provider does not know the pertinent information, here the dose range. She did not knowingly break a rule, and nothing about her hands or the equipment caused the error.
questions.question: A new EMT draws up the wrong dose of a medication because she genuinely did not know the correct dose range. She was not rushing, and she believed she was following the protocol correctly. Reviewers classify this error as:

questions.explanation: State office of EMS: The state-level office that typically regulates the standards for prehospital emergency care and the individuals who provide it.
questions.question: Which term is defined as: The state-level office that typically regulates the standards for prehospital emergency care and the individuals who provide it.

questions.explanation: The state office of EMS is the state-level office that regulates the standards for prehospital care and the individuals who provide it, including discipline of a state credential. The National Registry certifies, but it does not suspend a state credential.
questions.question: An EMT is accused of practicing outside his scope, and the state-issued credential he practices under is now under review for possible suspension. Which body has the authority to suspend it?

questions.explanation: EMT licensure/employment requirements: The criteria a person must meet to become licensed and employed as an EMT, which include proof of immunization against certain communicable diseases.
questions.question: Which term is defined as: The criteria a person must meet to become licensed and employed as an EMT, which include proof of immunization against certain communicable diseases.

choices: Proof of immunization against certain communicable diseases
questions.explanation: Proof of immunization is one of the criteria a person must meet to become licensed and employed as an EMT. College credits, a commercial license, and volunteer years are not part of those requirements.
questions.question: A candidate has passed her EMT course, her national exam, and her background check, and an agency is ready to hire her. One required item is still missing from her file, and it legally blocks the hire until she provides it. Which item is it?

choices: The state office of EMS's enforcement duties
EMT well-being, one of the human resources department's three areas
On-line medical control by the medical director
questions.explanation: EMT well-being is one of the human resources department's three areas (well-being, career progression, compensation); this agency built a dedicated wellness role to own it.
questions.question: In 2025, Virginia Beach EMS created a Health and Wellness Manager role reporting directly to the chief, after a Virginia survey found 82% of EMS providers had experienced burnout, traumatic stress, PTSD, depression, or similar impacts. Which department's area of responsibility does this role carry out?

choices: It replaces initial EMT training for new hires
It is only a paperwork requirement for keeping a certification
It is a disciplinary tool run by the state office of EMS
It maintains, updates, and expands provider knowledge, and is part of why providers are trusted with a wider scope of practice
questions.explanation: Continuing education is not paperwork; in King County it is part of why providers are trusted with a wider scope of practice.
questions.question: King County's continuing education program was reaccredited through CAPCE, and its Training and Education Section distributed ten new online CE courses for EMTs, paramedics, and telecommunicators. The county credits this ongoing training for letting its paramedics use an extensive array of medications and procedures. What does this show about continuing education?

choices: Accidental Death and Disability: The Neglected Disease of Modern Society, the white paper whose publication originated modern EMS
The Freedom House Ambulance training standard
questions.explanation: The 1966 white paper exposed how inadequate prehospital emergency care was; EMS as we know it today originated with its publication.
questions.question: A 1966 National Academy of Sciences / National Research Council report found that 52 million accidental injuries in 1965 killed 107,000 people, and that there was no standard for the competence or training of ambulance attendants. What is this document?
questions.topic: Accidental Death and Disability: The Neglected Disease of Modern Society

questions.explanation: Freedom House was the white paper era put into practice one year later: trained providers giving real emergency care before the hospital, instead of a ride only.
questions.question: In 1967 in Pittsburgh, a new ambulance service trained its crews for 32 weeks and more than 300 hours, covering anatomy, physiology, and CPR. In its first year it made 5,868 runs, and its crews are recognized as the nation's first paramedics. What was this service?

choices: A failure of the state office of EMS
A knowledge-based failure: the provider did not know the pertinent information and did not confirm it
An equipment failure in the syringe
A documentation failure after the call
questions.explanation: Before any drug is given, confirm medication, dose, and route out loud with your partner; if you do not know, stop and ask.
questions.question: In New Zealand in 2023, an EMT gave adrenaline intravenously from a syringe intended for the nebuliser route, without confirming the medication, dose, and route with the paramedic. The patient suffered a cardiac arrest. What type of failure was this?

choices: A state office of EMS, regulating the standards for prehospital care and the individuals who provide it
questions.explanation: MIEMSS is a state office of EMS doing exactly the textbook job: regulating care standards, training, and the individuals who provide care, statewide.
questions.question: Maryland's MIEMSS became an independent agency in 1993. It oversees and coordinates the statewide EMS system, licenses and regulates commercial ambulance services, and reviews and approves education programs. What is MIEMSS an example of?

choices: OSHA's vaccination offer to current employees
EMT licensure/employment requirements, which include proof of immunization against certain communicable diseases
State office of EMS disciplinary rules
questions.explanation: A real Texas EMT pipeline will not move an applicant forward without documented immunization or a titer proving immunity.
questions.question: A Texas EMT program run by TEEX requires applicants to submit proof of MMR and varicella vaccination (two doses or a positive titer), hepatitis B vaccination (three doses or a positive titer), and Tdap within the last ten years before the application moves forward. These requirements are part of what?

choices: Employment: hepatitis B protection is treated as part of starting work as an EMT
A state EMS office enforcement action
questions.explanation: Federal workplace law treats hepatitis B protection as part of starting work as an EMT, which is why proof of the series, a titer, or a signed declination follows the EMT into employment.
questions.question: Under OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens standard, employers must offer the hepatitis B vaccination series at no cost to emergency responders within 10 days of initial assignment, and a worker who declines must sign a written declination form. This requirement follows the EMT into what?
